title: Trade any for unknown
summary: Type a thin API client, argue about unknown, then walk the first answer back.

turns.user: want to get the any out of client.ts. start with get

assistant.body: Adding a type parameter so the caller names the shape. res.json hands back any, so I park it in an unknown first and cast once at the end, where you can actually see it.

turns.user: whats the actual difference vs unknown though. both of them take anything as far as i can tell

assistant.body: Going in they are the same. Coming out they are not. any flows anywhere and switches checking off, unknown does nothing until you narrow it. And as T is just you promising you narrowed it, so a wrong promise ends the checking too.

turns.user: ok drop the T then, just return unknown. and fix pick while you are in there

assistant.body: Fair. The type parameter I suggested lets the caller lie, which puts it about where any was. get goes back to returning unknown, and pick takes the value type instead so indexing gives T | undefined.

sed -i '' -e 's/get(url: string): Promise<any>/get(url: string): Promise<unknown>/' -e 's/pick(data: any, key: string): any/pick<T>(data: Record<string, T>, key: string): T | undefined/' src/api/client.ts
